query: What happens if it stops making insulin?
answer: If the pancreas stops making insulin, glucose can't move out of the blood and into the body's cells, so blood sugar climbs too high (hyperglycemia) [1]. That's what happens in type 1 diabetes: the immune system destroys the insulin-making beta cells, and high blood sugar usually appears once about 80–90% of them are gone [2][1]. Early signs include a lot of thirst, frequent urination, weight loss and tiredness [1]. Because the cells can't use sugar for energy, the body breaks down fat instead and makes ketones. This can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a life-threatening condition with very high blood sugar, acidic blood, dehydration and salt imbalances [3][2]. Without insulin, this is fatal. Today people manage it by taking insulin every day through injections or a pump [1].
